messages:
omar: Heads up — starting onboarding for bluefin-4b-community. License header says CC-BY-NC-4.0 but there's an extra paragraph about ‘no redistribution of raw model weights’ attached. Can legal confirm whether we can host a quantized variant behind Redwood Private?

rachel: thanks — is there a link to the license + model repo?

omar: https://example.com/bluefin-4b-community (repo) — license.txt pasted in root. key bits: ‘NonCommercial; no bulk redistribution; attribution required with model name and author handle’. Also a separate file: redistribution_policy.md that says “no distribution of weights in any binary form without explicit consent”.

jess: quick ML note — we planned to run 4-bit QAT / PTQ experiments. If the license forbids redistributing weights, is publishing a quantized checkpoint as an ‘artifact’ to customers considered redistribution?

legal-sara: Short answer: probably yes in plain reading, but need context. Two questions: 1) does the author define what counts as ‘redistribution’ (source vs derived weight)? 2) is hosting behind an authenticated API considered redistribution or mere hosting?

ben: from product perspective, typical flows: hosted API (we serve outputs only), Dedicated (customer gets reserved compute, we still hold weights), Private on-prem (customer gets weights/containers) — difference matters.

omar: for our use-case we were thinking Redwood Private (VPC image + customer-managed infra) where we ship a container with model weights to customer infra. That would definitely be redistribution unless we can do a bring-your-own-weights flow.

legal-sara: OK clear. If the license prohibits redistribution of weights, we have options: 1) contact upstream for a commercial license / redistribution carve-out, 2) do hosted-only offering (we keep weights, serve via API), 3) offer BYOW (customer supplies and we validate). Need to triage risk level.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: ensure artefact provenance tracking, KMS policies for keys, watermarking disabled for upstream IP.

omar: also discovered a weird attribution clause: must include author handle and a link to original repo in product UI where model name appears. That is doable for hosted UI, but complicated for API-only customers (no UI).

rachel: can we add attribution to request/response headers? probably not visible to end-users. For hosted console we can add footer. For Dedicated, customers modify UI. But license might require downstream attribution regardless of access surface.

legal-sara: We should do a short memo to upstream asking clarifying Qs: 1) definition of redistribution/derivative weights 2) whether quantized variants are considered derivatives or redistributed artifacts 3) whether hosting behind auth counts as redistribution 4) acceptable attribution mechanisms for API-only use. I'll draft and cc product.

jess: ML question to add: if quantization changes weights format substantially (4-bit packed tensors), some licensors still treat it as 'derivative' — please ask whether format transformation qualifies as derivative vs permitted transform.

omar: also ran quick evals — dl-eval-bot posted a regression in our translation test after 4-bit PTQ: bleu down 2.4 pts vs fp16 baseline. Not huge but needs to be documented in onboarding.

ld-eval-bot: (automated) evaluation summary: model=bluefin-4b-community, baseline=fp16, ptq=4-bit, dataset=internal-translations-v2, bleu: 28.7 -> 26.3, latency p50 +18%, memory footprint -45%. Full logs: https://ci.example/bluefin-4b/ptq-run-2245309876

ben: thanks — from a go-to-market note: if we can only host (no redistribute), we should surface performance/cost numbers prominently so enterprise teams choose hosted vs Dedicated. Also need legal-approved copy for attribution.

legal-sara: I'll pull the exact license text and flag ambiguous clauses. If upstream is unresponsive within 5 business days we'll classify as ‘hosted-only allowed’ and block any redistrib in onboarding checklist. Also recommend adding a gating task: ‘redistribution clearance obtained’ before any Private/Dedicated deploy that packages weights.

omar: sounds good. I'll add a checklist entry to the model-onboarding board and attach the eval artifacts and license snapshots.

rachel: one more ops question — if we offer BYOW, what minimal verification do we need? model hash, provenance metadata, compatible runtime checks?

legal-sara: BYOW reduces our redistribution risk but increases liability if we fail to detect tainted weights. Ops should require: signed hash from customer, license attestation, and container-level scanning. We'll write specific acceptance criteria.

omar: ok wrapping up — next steps: legal-sara to send upstream questions + draft gating policy; jess to document quantization regression and add to onboarding notes; ben to update product positioning for hosted-only fallback. I'll update the thread when I have upstream reply. :thumbsup:
